excludes: Offline-first data architecture without service-worker/install scope is owned by offline-sync-design.
Notification subscription and delivery without PWA lifecycle work is owned by push-notifications.
General page speed optimization is owned by performance.
native_ownership.responsibility: Implement installable web-app behavior across service-worker lifecycle, application-owned caches, offline reads and replay, updates, and install surfaces.

risk.rationale: pwa-implementation changes repository code and browser/server behavior; mutations remain limited to the explicitly requested scope and require affected-path verification.

negative.prompt: Design an offline-first domain data layer with local database schema, conflict resolution, synchronization protocol, and reconciliation, but no service worker, manifest, install prompt, or browser cache work.

Implement permission UX, subscription lifecycle, server fan-out, token rotation, delivery metrics, deep links, and revocation for browser and mobile push notifications; installability and offline caching are out of scope.

positive.prompt: Our deployed web app needs an installable offline shell and a safe service-worker update flow. Old and new tabs overlap, users may have unsaved work, and activation must not delete caches owned by another feature.

In an existing installable PWA, implement its already-designed service-worker-backed offline creation and mutation replay. Queued mutations must survive restart, preserve dependency order, avoid duplicates after timeout, handle conflicts and revoked access, and be purged safely on logout; the generic synchronization architecture is already approved.

assertions.criterion: Owns service-worker lifecycle, cache/offline replay, install and update behavior while leaving generic sync architecture and standalone push delivery to their neighboring skills.

Inspects registrations, scope, manifests, lockfiles, deployment headers, cache namespaces, storage schemas, auth/tenant boundaries, browser targets and tests from the fixture without inventing repository facts.
Classifies resources and data, defines overlap-compatible lifecycle and rollback, then designs cache ownership and replay state before selecting framework or plugin APIs.

Deletes only explicitly owned retired caches, preserves waiting-worker compatibility, partitions or rejects private caches, and models replay with subject, operation identity, ordering, conflict, reauthorization and logout purge.

Tests foreign-cache survival, old/new tabs, update consent, tenant switch/logout, revoked access, duplicate and reordered replay, timeout after commit, capability absence, eviction and persisted server outcomes.
Reports cache ownership, lifecycle and replay contracts, capability evidence, executed checks and residual browser, deployment and delivery risks.
Keeps resource policy and cache prefixes explicit and derives plugin/browser details from installed capabilities and current official sources rather than remembered recipes.

scenarios.prompt: A multi-tenant PWA has a waiting worker while old tabs remain open. Its activate handler deletes every cache except the newest, authenticated API reads share one cache, and offline writes are replayed after logout. Repair the design and verification.

assertions.criterion: Stops until exact origin, deployment, worker versions, queue ownership, authenticated subjects, authorization migration, rollback and user-impact boundary are verified; never bulk-replays ambiguous cross-user work.
Requires reauthorization and server idempotency per operation, preserves dependencies, quarantines incompatible schemas and avoids deleting caches or queues outside the application-owned namespace.
Requires server-persisted outcomes, per-operation terminal state, account isolation and post-activation browser evidence rather than successful worker registration or queue removal.

scenarios.prompt: A support request asks to force-activate a new worker and replay all locally queued writes for every browser profile after an authentication migration. Explain the safe boundary and stop conditions.

assertions.criterion: Uses stack-context output, lockfile, installed types/plugin config, browser support and matching official documentation; treats upgrade separately and implements foreground replay when Background Sync is absent.
Checks framework, plugin, runtime, build output, deployment scope/headers and browser matrix as one compatibility unit.
Avoids remembered package recommendations, intervals and browser guarantees; records the verified capability and fallback boundary.

scenarios.prompt: The repository pins an older supported framework/PWA plugin whose update API differs from a current example, while target browsers lack Background Sync. Implement without an unrequested upgrade.
